findings.rootCause: PackedDomainFacts.widen ORed kindBits and languageBits (0|x = x) and intersect ANDed them (kind AND == 0 -> STATE_EMPTY, language AND silently 0) although in this encoding 0 means 'unknown' (PackedPredicateRange.reset zeroes everything; every verdict fires on non-zero bits). VALUES-seeded facts (PackedQueryCodec.seedBindingSetAssignmentFact) set kinds only, and LmdbPackedPredicateRangeProvider emits kinds=LITERAL with languageBits=0 when the RdfTermDomain has neither language fact, so widening `{ VALUES ?o {"a"@en} } UNION { ?s :p ?o }` (or two stored predicates) against a LANGUAGE_WITHOUT range produced a proof that every row is a language-free literal: langMatchesVerdict -> EmptySet for langMatches(lang(?o),'*'), languageVerdict -> tautology for lang(?o)='' (filter dropped). Audit item (4) of the design additionally found one unguarded consumer: the IS_NUMERIC rangeVerdict returned ALWAYS_FALSE whenever (kindBits & KIND_LITERAL) == 0, which under the corrected join becomes reachable with kindBits == 0 (unknown), proving `{ ?s :p ?o } UNION { ?s :r ?o } FILTER(isNumeric(?o))` empty when :r's kinds are unknown.
findings.change: PackedDomainFacts: new static joinBits/meetBits helpers with the documented 0 = unknown/top convention; widen uses joinBits for kinds and languages (a non-literal side contributes the other side's language bits vacuously via literalLanguageBits); intersect uses meetBits, proves EMPTY only from two known disjoint kind sets, and treats known disjoint language classes as 'no literal admitted' (EMPTY when kinds == LITERAL, else drops KIND_LITERAL and leaves languages unknown). New PackedDomainFacts.describeFiniteValueSet derives kinds, LANGUAGE_WITH/WITHOUT and XSD datatype bits (unknown as soon as a language-free literal carries a non-XSD datatype) from an enumerated value set; PackedQueryCodec.seedBindingSetAssignmentFact uses it so VALUES facts stay precise (the datatypeVerdict tautology now additionally requires languageBits == LANGUAGE_WITHOUT, since datatype bits describe language-free literals only). Resumed-session addition: the IS_NUMERIC verdict in PackedLogicalRuleProgram.rangeVerdict now requires kinds != 0 before refuting (all other consumers - datatypeVerdict, languageVerdict, langMatchesVerdict, kindVerdict, valuePossiblyEqualsRange, expandAnchorValue, codec rangeAdmitsTerm - were audited and already guard kinds != 0 or test for a specific non-zero bit). Sound because every operation only loses proofs derived from unknown bits; store-provided LANGUAGE_WITHOUT proofs (PackedPredicateRangePlanningTest#languageAbsent*) are unchanged and still green.

findings.rootCause: PackedQueryCodec's fact/rule fixpoint called deriveGroupFacts for every relation id, including alternatives that logical rules appended to existing memo groups, and deriveGroupFacts wrote into relations.groupId(relationId) where PackedDomainFacts.put strengthens by intersection. The finite-anchor alternative JOIN(VALUES ?o {anchor}, input) of a FILTER(?o = 1) group therefore replaced the FILTER group's copyAll(child) fact by the anchor's finite set; the enclosing JOIN with `?t :w ?o` intersected {1} with the stored {1.0} by object id -> STATE_EMPTY -> addEmptyDomainJoinAlternative emitted EmptySet for the whole join, and a sibling datatype FILTER's rangeVerdict read the poisoned range. The intersection is only sound under the memo invariant that all group members are equivalent, which any rule bug (3.2.4a/b) violates; PackedBindingFacts already derives from the first member only.
findings.change: PackedQueryCodec.deriveGroupFacts returns immediately unless relations.groupId(relationId) == relationId (the seed expression that opened the group; PackedExpressionInterner.internCanonical assigns size+1 as the group id, so alternatives added via internLogicalIfSameGroup are never their own group). Alternatives consume facts (their children are seeds of their own groups) but never produce them; documented on deriveGroupFacts and in the PackedDomainFacts class javadoc. Per the critique (minor 3.2.4c), the one sound narrowing that used to leak in through the FINITE_FILTER_VALUES alternative is re-derived seed-side: the FILTER case now calls PackedLogicalRuleProgram.deriveFilterDomainFacts, which intersects the child fact with the filter's finite constants when collectFiniteDomain accepts the condition (EQUALITY_COMPARISON / LIST_MEMBER / OR of those on one variable) and every constant is term-identity exact (IRI, bnode, xsd:string; language-tagged literals are deliberately excluded here because their value-equality class can hold several terms). Unbound rows are dropped by such filters in every mode, so the fact 'unbound or in the finite set' holds for the group. Consequence: an unsound alternative can only mis-plan itself, never siblings or parents; disjoint-join emptiness proofs for string/IRI IN-lists are preserved (PackedSeedOnlyDomainFactsTest#termIdentitySafeFilterConstantsStillProveDisjointJoinEmpty).

findings.rootCause: PackedLogicalRuleProgram.expandAnchorValue's finite-domain fallback replaced FILTER(?o = c) by JOIN(VALUES ?o {expanded}, input) - a term-identity join - but selected the stored terms with stored.equals(value), i.e. RDF term identity. With a finite stored domain {"1"^^integer, "01"^^integer, "1.0"^^decimal, 2} and FILTER(?o = 1) only "1"^^integer was anchored and the two value-equal rows were lost (LmdbPackedPredicateRangeProvider emits finite domains when RdfTermDomain.isFinite(), so reachable e2e). The same fallback is reached by VALUES-seeded finite facts arriving through a sibling JOIN or UNION widening.
findings.change: New expandFiniteAnchorValue selects stored finite values by SPARQL value equality exactly as the filter decides it: each stored term is compared with QueryEvaluationUtility.compare(stored, constant, EQ, strict) in both strict and extended mode; included iff both are _true; the whole expansion is refused (-1) when the modes disagree (calendar/duration promotion, per the critique the refuse branch is required, covered by durationConstantWhoseEqualityDependsOnComparisonModeIsNeitherAnchoredNorProvedEmpty and dateTimeConstantAgainstFiniteDateDomainPreservesResults), on illegalArgument, or on a thrown comparison error; _false/incompatible terms are excluded because the filter drops those rows in every mode (false or type error). Because every exclusion is definite, an expansion that admits no stored term is now a proof that the constant matches no row (EmptySet), replacing the old `count == expandedCount ? -1` tail; this is the same finite-fact completeness exposure as existing PREDICATE_RANGE_EMPTY proofs (wp3 note). Language-tag case variants ("a"@en vs "a"@EN) are both anchored.

findings.rootCause: PackedLogicalRuleProgram.addFiniteCodeTypeAlternative rewrites the code/type UNION under COUNT(DISTINCT) into JOIN(JOIN(VALUES code, VALUES type), JOIN(?e a ?type, ?e :code ?c)), dropping the FILTER(?c = ?t || ?c = 3) and matching ?c against the collected codes by term identity; appendBranchCodeValue only checked `instanceof Value`, so a stored "1.0"^^xsd:decimal that value-equals the integer code 1 in the FILTER was not matched by the join and the entity was lost (count 1 instead of 2). The finite-filter rule guards exactly this through finiteDomainTermIdentitySafe (string/langString only); the code/type rule never did. PackedRewriteBindingSafetyTest#finiteTypeDomainPreservesNumericValueEquality used xsd:int on both sides and so only exercised term-equal numerics.
findings.change: Extracted static termIdentitySafe(Object) (IRI, bnode, xsd:string or rdf:langString literal) and used it both in finiteDomainTermIdentitySafe and, per the critique, inside appendBranchCodeValue so that both branch offsets and the disjunction literal are covered: any numeric, boolean or temporal code constant declines the FINITE_CODE_TYPE_VALUES rewrite. String, IRI and language-tagged codes keep the rewrite (PackedCodeTypeTermIdentityTest#stringCodesKeepTheRewrite etc., PackedRewriteBindingSafetyTest#finiteTypeDomainUsesFreshBindingNames unchanged). Strengthened PackedRewriteBindingSafetyTest#finiteTypeDomainPreservesNumericValueEquality to xsd:integer codes against a stored "1.0"^^xsd:decimal so it now requires the guard.
